limitations: Finite Hann-window leakage remains outside harmonic guards; this energy is not a direct alias-power measurement.
Aliases coinciding with harmonic guards are counted as harmonic; low frequencies and overlapping guards can leave few off-harmonic bins.
No universal aliasing, audibility, hardware, host, or superiority claim follows from these bounded cases.
Only lane0 of the three stationary spectrum cases and declared later windows is analyzed; all startup frames remain part of the separate numerical qualification.
An interpolated local peak estimates frequency; DC filtering, reconstruction, window leakage and nearby content can bias it.

metric_definition.dc_policy: exclude bins0..3 inclusive from analyzed AC denominator and numerator; separately report their energy; no subtraction of sample mean
metric_definition.fundamental: largest bin near requested frequency within max(2 bins,2% requested); log-power parabolic interpolation using its immediate neighbors, limited ±0.5bin; null if local power is zero; this is a local frequency estimate, not general pitch detection
metric_definition.gate: none; every valid measured value is reported, with no threshold or SDK-vs-Rust spectral pass/fail
metric_definition.harmonic_policy: positive integer multiples of each trace waveform measured fundamental through Nyquist; union integer bins within ±3 bins of each fractional center; no folded harmonics
metric_definition.input_decoding: decimal trace tokens rounded to canonical IEEE754 binary32 before promotion to Python double for windowing and FFT; serializer decimal precision is not measured signal
metric_definition.off_harmonic: analyzed AC power outside that union; fraction and10log10 ratio relative to all analyzed AC power; null ratio if denominator zero and null dB if numerator zero
metric_definition.power: one-sided |DFT(x*window)|^2/(N*sum(window^2)); double interior bins, retain DC/Nyquist once; units V^2

revised_qualification.basis: Original immutable declaration plus versioned float32 phase-endpoint erratum; not a pass against the original open-interval invariant
